thread.title: Audit finds achievement gaps in Blount County Schools - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Audit finds achievement gaps in Blount County Schools - NewsBreak

author: Shanon Adame
title: Audit finds achievement gaps in Blount County Schools - NewsBreak
text: The Blount County school board recently heard the results of a district-wide curriculum audit, ordered by the board. CSMi Auditors Kay Coleman and Steven Ebell presented their findings to the board on May 8. Coleman and Ebell broke the findings into five focus areas: District Vision and Accountability, Curriculum, Consistency and Equity, Feedback and Productivity. The Daily Times will report on each of the audit’s five focus areas. Focus Area Four (Feedback): “The school district uses the results from system-designed and/or adopted assessments to adjust, improve, or terminate ineffective practices or programs.” According to the report, auditors examined the overall scope and quality of the district’s assessment system for use in decision-making. Auditors said a district meeting the standards for Focus Area Four would have designed a comprehensive system of assessment and testing, and would use “valid measurement tools” that indicate how well students are achieving goals and objectives. Finding 4.3 “Students in Blount County Schools perform at or above the state level on most high-stakes assessments; however, some results have fallen below the state average. Significant achievement gaps exist in these assessment results for some student groups.” According to the report, to calculate student outcome trends, auditors reviewed state and district policies/plans, Tennessee State Report Card data and documents provided by the district. They also surveyed administrators, teachers and parents. Auditors said they found that the district’s students have performed “slightly above the state average on the state-required assessments for English language arts, mathematics, science, and social studies,” but that recent data showed students beginning to fall in all areas except science. The report stated that students who are “economically disadvantaged” are performing above the state average when compared to similar students, but are underperforming when compared to “non-economically disadvantaged” students in the district. English learners and students with disabilities are performing below the state average, the report said. Auditors also stated that achievement gaps exist for Hispanic and Black/African American students. According to the report, district leaders provided auditors with data from assessments. Auditors said they chose to focus on results from the Tennessee Comprehensive Assessment Program and iReady Diagnostic Screener. “When possible, auditors analyzed assessment results for all students, special education students, and those identified as economically disadvantaged English learners,” the report read. District and Tennessee student demographicsWhen analyzing TCAP results, auditors said they compared campuses in the district at all grade levels. The report stated that 14% of the district’s students are classified as economically disadvantaged and the district enrolled fewer English learner students than the State of Tennessee. It also said the district enrolled 85% White students, larger than the state average, and fewer Hispanic and Black/African American students. Student comparison with statewide performance on TCAPsAccording to the report, students scoring “met” or “exceeding expectations” saw a decline after COVID-19 but have been stable since 2022. Auditors said in the two years following COVID, student performance increased by a larger percentage than the state. Going into 2024, state scores increased to 49% while the district remained at 41%. In TCAP mathematics, both the district and state saw increases in 2022 and 2023; however, in 2024, the state continued to increase, and the district remained stable, auditors said. In science, the district has remained about two to five percentage points above the state average. For social studies, student performance increased from 40% to 45% from 2019 to 2024. District subgroup performance on TCAPAuditors said they analyzed TCAP performance for students who are classified as economically disadvantaged, English learners and students with disabilities. The report stated that economically disadvantaged students in the district consistently performed higher than the state average in English and math. It also said that the TCAP ELA performance of English learners and students with disabilities has “consistently been below the state.” In science and social studies, economically disadvantaged students in the district perform higher than the state average, the report said. English learners, however, perform consistently below state average. Auditors said students with disabilities have performed consistently with the state, but that they are starting to show a decline. Trend Analysis for subgroups According to the report, “Student groups in Blount County Schools consistently perform lower than their non-identified peers, creating significant achievement gaps.” Auditors said, when looking at trends in achievement between Hispanic, Black/African American and White students, that the gap for math will never close for Black/African American students without intervention. For Hispanic students, they said it would take three years to close the gap if instruction is not changed. For reading, auditors said without intervention, the gap would never close for Black/African American students, and that the gap could close in six years for Hispanic students. Auditors said that, based on past performance, without intervention, it would take 18 years to close gaps in ELA and 13 years in math. High School outcomesAuditors said that the district’s four-year graduation rate is consistently over 90% for all students and has maintained a higher graduation rate than the state from 2019 to 2023. All three subgroups graduate at a higher rate than the state, the report said. “Creating a plan to analyze student achievement data by conducting trend analysis for student groups will enable district leaders to support staff in communicating data-informed decisions to positively impact student learning,” auditors wrote.
